issues.description: import-notation 'url' primary may incorrectly skip strings containing 'url(' substring
issues.detail: In lib/rules/import-notation/index.mjs, when primary === 'url', the code returns early if params matches /url\(/i. However, '@import "foo url(bar)"' is a string literal whose textual content includes 'url(' but is not a real url() call. The previous implementation would parse the value and correctly flag it as needing conversion; the new fast-path returns without checking. This is a contrived but real behavioral regression — the optimization changes outcomes rather than just skipping known-clean inputs.

Previously the check used `selector.includes(':not(')` which is case-sensitive; the new walkRules filter is `/:not\(/i` (case-insensitive). Selectors written as ':NOT(' or ':Not(' would now enter the rule body whereas they were silently skipped before. CSS pseudo-class names are case-insensitive per spec, so this is arguably a correctness improvement, but it is an undocumented behavior change that could expand the set of warnings users see and is not called out in the changeset.

issues.description: HAS_NAMED / HAS_NUMERIC regexes are built from sets without escaping
issues.detail: In font-weight-notation/index.mjs the regex sources are joined directly from `fontWeightNonNumericKeywords`, `fontWeightRelativeKeywords`, and NUMERIC_TO_NAMED keys. These are all plain identifiers/digits today, so no regex metacharacters are present, but the construction has no defense-in-depth: if any future keyword were added containing a metacharacter (e.g., a hyphen or dot in an extended set), the precompiled regex would silently mis-match. A small `escapeRegExp` helper on each token would harden this.

issues.description: keyframe-selector-notation HAS_PERCENTAGE regex lacks anchored end and 'i' flag
issues.detail: HAS_PERCENTAGE = /(?:^|[,\s])(?:0%|25%|...)/ — there is no trailing boundary, so '0%5' (not a valid selector but possible via SCSS interpolation passing through) could match. Also no `i` flag, whereas HAS_KEYWORD uses /i. Percentages are case-insensitive (no letters anyway) so the missing flag is benign, but the asymmetry is worth a comment. As a coarse pre-filter the looseness only costs optimization, not correctness.

issues.description: selector-pseudo-element-colon-notation walkRules(/:/) filter is extremely broad
issues.detail: The new filter `/:/` matches any selector containing a colon, including very common pseudo-classes (`:hover`, `:focus`, `:nth-child(...)`). Most stylesheets will see no real filtering benefit from this change versus the original `selector.includes(':')` short-circuit, since walkRules still iterates all matching rules. The performance win is real (one regex test per rule vs string includes) but smaller than the other rules in this PR; worth confirming with benchmarks the changeset alludes to.

issues.description: No new tests added to lock down the early-return behavior
issues.detail: The diff contains no test changes. Each new fast-path is a behavioral surface — particularly the import-notation `/url\(/i` filter and the case-insensitive `:not(` filter — that could regress silently. Existing tests presumably still pass because they cover canonical inputs; targeted tests for the skip conditions (value contains `url(` inside a string, selector with `:NOT(`, font shorthand with `100%` size) would prevent future regressions.

Any params containing a substring `min-` or `max-` (case-insensitive) will pass the filter, including identifiers in custom media queries (e.g., `(--min-width-breakpoint)`). This only costs optimization, not correctness, and matches the pre-PR behavior of running the full check, so it is acceptable. A tighter pattern like /\b(?:min|max)-(?:width|height|resolution|aspect-ratio|color|monochrome|device-...)/ would be safer but coupled to the feature list.

dissents.topic: Is the import-notation 'url' fast-path actually incorrect?

positions.position: It is a behavioral regression: '@import "... url( ..."' (string form with url( inside) would have been flagged under primary='url' before and is now silently skipped. Performance optimizations must not change outputs. P1.

Such an @import value is nonsensical CSS and no real-world stylesheet contains it. The optimization is correct for all realistic inputs and the rest of the rule still validates the URL form when it runs. P2 at most.
CSS pseudo-class names are ASCII case-insensitive per the selectors spec; the old `includes(':not(')` was a pre-existing minor bug and this change fixes it. Mention in changeset.
The PR is scoped to performance, not behavior. Silently widening match scope risks new warnings in users' codebases on upgrade. Should be split into a separate change or at least called out.

dissents.topic: Whether unescaped regex construction is worth flagging

positions.position: Always escape tokens before joining into a regex; future keyword additions could break this silently.
All current sources are constants of plain identifiers and digits. Escaping is dead code that adds noise; add it only when a non-identifier keyword is actually introduced.

review.summary: The PR adds early-return fast paths to seven *-notation rules to avoid expensive value/selector parsing when the rule could not possibly fire. The approach is sound and consistent with existing selector-* rules. One issue is worth attention before merge: the import-notation `primary === 'url'` filter uses `/url\(/i.test(params)`, which can match the substring `url(` inside a string-literal @import value and incorrectly skip a real violation. Two smaller behavior changes are undocumented: `selector-not-notation` switches from case-sensitive `includes(':not(')` to case-insensitive `/:not\(/i`, and several regexes are constructed without escaping their source tokens. No tests were added to cover the new skip paths. Overall the change is acceptable and high-value, but the import-notation edge case and the case-sensitivity change deserve either a code adjustment, a test, or an explicit note in the changeset.
